anti_overlap: Does not review salience decay mathematics or the gossip-consumer mechanism (see fd-broadcast-archives-lexeme-legibility)
Does not review ECS storage split or component boundary decisions (those are implementation concerns, not conferral-governance concerns)
Does not review farewell narrative prose quality, only that the farewell system has access to the correct epithet record
decision_lens: Heraldic registries codify exactly what act earns an augmentation and who adjudicates boundary cases — the same problem as defining 'rivalry peak' for the Defiant or 'legendary via music' for Silverstring. Cadency rules (how junior members of a house differentiate their display) map directly to the max-2-displayed, most-prestigious-first question.
distance_rationale: Heraldry is a medieval identity-labeling institution, not a software system, but it has solved the same problem — earned, displayable, precedence-ordered identity markers — for centuries, with formal rules for disambiguation and conflict resolution.
expected_isomorphisms: Heraldic blazon precision maps to trigger-condition specification; cadency rules for display in constrained space map to the max-2-display and sort-key decisions; the permanent-grant principle maps to the requirement that earned epithets never vanish from the internal record.
focus: Apply heraldic registry practice to evaluate the conferral conditions, precedence ordering, and display rules for earned epithets
name: fd-heraldic-registry-epithet-conferral
persona: Apply the perspective of a herald at a medieval armorial registry — they care about the precision of earning conditions (blazon rules), the governance of display order (rule of tincture, cadency), and whether a bearer's granted arms are distinguishable and non-colliding. They flag ambiguous grant conditions that could produce disputes, and they scrutinize whether prestige ordering is coherent when an elf earns multiple arms.
review_areas: Blazon precision for 'the Defiant': heraldic practice demands that earning conditions be unambiguous enough that a third party can adjudicate a disputed claim — is 'rivalry intensity >= 0.8 at composition tick' specific enough, or does it leave a dispute window analogous to contested arms?

Collision detection for Silverstring: if prestige is global rather than domain-scoped, every Legendary elf earns Silverstring — a heraldic 'conflict' where multiple bearers carry identical arms, which registries reject. Flag that domain-scoped prestige is a prerequisite for Silverstring to carry meaning.

Cadency logic for max-2-display: heraldic cadency determines which variant is shown when space is constrained. The brainstorm resolves this as 'sort by salience desc, earned_tick asc' — evaluate whether salience (cultural recency) is the right cadency key, or whether prestige_score (earned rank) should take precedence over temporal decay for the owner's own display.

Posthumous and permanent-grant semantics: in heraldry, arms persist after death and are never revoked. The brainstorm says epithets persist internally even when off the 2-slot display — verify that the implementation never drops an EarnedEpithet from the Vec, and that farewell narrative always has access to the full earned record, not just the display cache.

Augmentation of honour vs. ordinary arms: heraldry distinguishes epithets granted by an authority from those self-assumed. The brainstorm's event-reactor pattern is authority-granted (the system confers on trigger); flag whether there is any guard against an elf 'self-earning' an epithet via a replayed or fabricated event.

Multi-epithet display order legibility: a coat that is too complex is considered unreadable at a distance ('tincture rule'). With two epithets displayed simultaneously, evaluate whether 'Lirael the Defiant Silverstring' reads clearly, and whether the display helper should insert punctuation or conjunctions to keep legibility.

severity_examples.condition: If PrestigeTier::Legendary has no domain field, every elf who reaches Legendary earns Silverstring — heraldic conflict, the epithet loses distinguishing function
severity_examples.scenario: Silverstring is awarded to all Legendary elves because prestige is global, not music-domain-scoped

severity_examples.condition: An epithet bumped by gossip references (+2 salience) overtakes an elder epithet with lower residual salience — display ordering does not reflect actual earned standing
severity_examples.scenario: Salience-based cadency causes a recently-gossiped minor epithet to displace an older, more prestigious one in the display slot

severity_examples.condition: Event bus drains multiple ArtCompleted events for the same elf in one pass — earned Vec grows duplicate entries; display and farewell text repeat the same epithet
severity_examples.scenario: No guard against duplicate epithet conferral if the triggering event fires twice in one tick

success_hints: Require domain-scoped prestige before Silverstring can fire; treat global-prestige as a blocking P1
Separate 'display prestige order' (for the elf's own rendered name) from 'colony salience order' (for gossip system consumption) — they may warrant different sort keys
Add a dedup guard in the epithet-conferral path: check earned Vec before inserting, keyed on epithet variant (not on LexemeId)
Verify that farewell narrative reads from the full earned Vec, not the 2-slot display cache, so elders with 3+ epithets get the most historically significant one in their sendoff
task_context: Review the earned-epithet conferral system and display ordering decisions in the brainstorm, applying heraldic registry standards for earning-condition precision, display hierarchy, and collision-free grant semantics.
